correctness.rationale: From the specified harmonic isometries, summing the Fourier terms for a nonzero difference gives diagonal entries ±1/10 and upper-right (3/10)(τ_k/√11)χ_k(b−a). For the nontrivial multiplicative character, squaring the Gauss-sum modulus and grouping pairs by their ratio gives 11: the inner additive sum is 10 at ratio one and −1 elsewhere. A common diagonal gauge therefore removes the phase. The blocks are Hermitian because χ_k is even, and their squares before division by 10 are 10I₂. Affine translation preserves differences and dilation supplies only one common removable phase. Acting on each block by J followed by conjugation negates every traceless Hermitian block and pairs real eigenvalues of B with their negatives, so its polynomial is Q(X²) with nonnegative squared roots. Independent exact subset determinants over Z[ω] verified the four rows, and disjoint affine orbits of sizes 55,110,110,55 exhaust 330 selections. Galois substitution in the sole real generator ω²+ω³ gives t₋ for k=1,4 and t₊ for k=2,3. Exact negative evaluations at L and positivity of every upper-shift coefficient exclude all larger roots outside the certified intervals. In class one the largest root is >77 and all other orbit maxima are <57 or <52 or <43; in class two it is >67.9 and the other maxima are <63, <67.3 and <66. The strict separation gives exactly the two claimed equality orbits. Since the winning upper brackets are <100, all Grams are positive definite. The sharp minimum is 1−δ and worst spectral Gram condition is (1+δ)/(1−δ); numerical re-evaluation gives δ≈0.8807235348056768 and 0.8242260805290105 and reproduces the displayed condition numbers.
residual_risks: Exact finite arithmetic for F₁₁ and the stated characters. Numerical approximations illustrate, not certify, the exact root ordering. The condition number is that of the Gram matrix, not a general reconstruction or noise guarantee.

value.rationale: Four-block Gram stability is a motivated erasure invariant not captured by pairwise angles. Entire finite spectral and equality data for a natural harmonic family quantify a nontrivial split even between Galois-related choices and change which affine configurations are worst. The optimal min-eigenvalues and spectral condition numbers describe concrete conditioning for every four-plane selection.
residual_risks: This is scoped complete data at one field order, not a general theorem about fusion frames or arbitrary erasure models.
